title: Launch Horizon Mapping and Capacity Primer
content:
Purpose:
This is a short, pragmatic primer to anchor the upcoming product roadmap sprint to a launch-ready runway. Focus is on: the single critical path ("Horizon"), the KPI anchors that decide go/no-go, and the capacity + contingency plan that keeps latency and cost within SLOs during ramp.

TL;DR (for execs):
- Primary launch horizon: progressive beta -> limited GA over 8 weeks starting 2025-04-15.
- Critical path items: dedicated model version pinning, routing fallback policy, first-100k-token cost profile, canary traffic gating.
- KPIs to lock before gradual ramp: 95th pct latency <= 450ms for 256-token median, error rate < 0.5%  (infra + model combo), cost per 1k tokens within 15% of forecast.
- Contingency: staged rollback to lightweight model variant + prefix cache warmup; capacity buffer = +30% reserved GPUs for first 72 hours.

Audience and how to use this doc:
- Product ops to coordinate cross-functional owners and run the daily readiness checkpoint.
- Eng and SRE to validate capacity and observability hooks.
- Customer success and Solutions to prepare runbooks and de-risk support handoffs.
- This doc is intentionally tactical; link out to the canonical Confluence planning page for long-form decision history (see linked_artifacts).

1) Roadmap Horizon (critical path)
- Week 0 (2025-04-15): internal canary (10% traffic) after model pin + routing policy deployed.
- Week 1: expand canary to 25% if KPIs stable.
- Week 3: limited GA (invited customers), traffic 1k requests/min sustained tests.
- Week 5-6: open GA (phased regions), monitoring and cost validation.
- Week 8: full GA and commit to reserved capacity schedule.

Critical path checklist (order matters):
- [ ] Model pinning PR merged (console + API) — owner: Diego Morales — JIRA: INF-1279
- [ ] Routing fallback matrix validated in staging — owner: Rae Chen — JIRA: POPS-842
- [ ] Observability hooks (per-route latency, token-level cost) enabled and dashboards ready — owner: SRE oncall rotation (SRE lead: Sofiya Ivanov)
- [ ] Cost rehearsal run (simulation of 100k tokens/min for 30m) with billing probe — owner: Finance ops (request: Billing-ops)
- [ ] Canary automation and gating scripts in release repo — owner: Release engineering

2) KPI tracker (anchors to verify during canary and expand phases)
- KPI: 95th percentile token latency (256 token context target)
  - Target: <= 450ms
  - Measurement: production tracing + canary dashboard
  - Gate: fail if > 600ms for 15m sliding window
- KPI: Error rate (5xx + timeouts)
  - Target: < 0.5%
  - Gate: fail if > 1% over 10m window
- KPI: Cost per 1k tokens (hosted) vs forecast
  - Target: within +15% of forecast model
  - Gate: pause expansion if > +30% for sustained 1h and investigate quantization/configs
- KPI: KV/prefix cache hit rate (latency proxy)
  - Target: >= 70% for typical prompts
  - Gate: if < 50% re-evaluate cache warmup scripts and routing
- KPI: End-to-end request time (client -> response)
  - Target: 90th pct <= 700ms

3) Capacity and cost assumptions (baseline model cluster)
- Baseline traffic profile (expected first 2 weeks): 200 rps average, 5 concurrent tokens per request avg, median sequence 128 tokens.
- GPU baseline: 12x A100-ish equivalent reserved for early GA (estimate supports ~10k rps with batching heuristics off peak).
- Buffer policy: +30% reserved for first 72 hours after each expansion step; auto-burst allowed but throttled by policy.
- Cache assumptions: warmup takes ~10 minutes per most-active prefix set; pre-warm can reduce observed latency by ~25%.
- Cost model notes: quantized variant reduces cost per token by ~20% but increases variance in latency. Use only as fallback in burst conditions.

4) Canary and expansion rules (operational playbook)
- Canary start: route 10% of baseline production traffic to new rollout lane. Run for minimum 30m and observe KPIs.
- If all KPIs green for 30m -> expand to 25% for 90m.
- If any gate trips during canary: immediate automatic rollback to previous stable variant AND page SRE + oncall product ops.
- Manual override: Product ops lead may pause expansion despite green KPIs (business reasons). Log reason in the launch channel.

5) Rollback and graceful degradation plan
- Fast rollback: switch model routing to last-stable model variant (console API toggle) and return all traffic. Expected < 60s to switch, verify health checks.
- Degrade lane: configure fallback to a smaller quantized variant with strict token limits (e.g., max 512 tokens) and circuit-breaker to avoid cost runaway.
- Communication: send incident notice to #launch-ops and SOC if degradation > 5m. Customer success to pre-seed messages for invited customers.

6) Monitoring runbook (what to watch, who watches it)
- Dashboards to watch: per-route latency, token-cost breakout, error-rate funnel, cache-hit heatmap, queue depth.
- Alerts: 95th latency breach, error rate spike, sudden cost delta > +20% over 10m.
- Who watches: product-ops (day shift), SRE (24/7 rotation), on-call eng for model team.
- Post-launch 24/72/168 checkpoints: daily runbook for first day (every 2h), twice daily for days 2-3, daily up to 7 days; summarize and publish to Confluence.

7) Communications and stakeholder triggers
- Pre-canary: 24h notice to Sales/CS and Solutions; prepare support scripts.
- On canary start: notify internal #launch-ops with link to canary dashboard + owners.
- On expand to GA: notify execs + customer success with adoption kit.

8) Dependencies and blockers (current)
- Model performance regression test suite flaky on long sequences — JIRA: INF-1834. Owner: Research.
- Billing-probe hook not yet plumbed into billing queue for simulated traffic — JIRA: FIN-62. Owner: Billing ops.
- Canary automation needs a small patch to routing policy API (PR pending) — GITHUB PR referenced above. Owner: Release engineering.

9) Open questions / notes to self
- Q: Do we expose explicit cost-to-customer signal in early GA? (pros: transparency; cons: complexity in support). Need Sales input.
- Q: Is a soft cap on token length required for first 2 weeks? If yes, require UI/SDK flag and docs.
- Note: prepare an abridged customer-facing FAQ for invited GA customers (template under linked artifacts).

10) Next actions (short term)
- Asha: follow-up with Release eng on PR status (due 2025-02-14).
- Diego: validate model pin performance in staging (target: 2025-02-20).
- Rae: finalize routing fallback matrix and add tests (target: 2025-02-22).
- Sofiya: provision additional +30% GPU buffer on reservation request and draft cost rehearsal schedule (target: 2025-02-18).

Appendix: quick quick-check cheat sheet for daily stand (copyable)
- Stand checklist (5 bullets, < 5 min):
  1) Are canary KPIs within gates? (latency / error / cost)
  2) Any alerts from SLO monitors in last 2h?
  3) Cache hit rate trending down? If yes, why?
  4) Are oncall owners on call? Any resource contention?
  5) Any customer-facing impact observed/tested?

——
Last updated 2025-03-01 by Asha Patel.
